text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a breast mass; could you please describe when you first noticed it and if you have experienced any associated pain or skin changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the mass feel fixed to the underlying tissue or chest wall, and have you noticed any nipple discharge or dimpling of the skin over the lump?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid growth and lack of skin changes, I need to rule out aggressive malignancies or inflammatory conditions. REQUEST TEST: Breast_Ultrasound and Mammogram.

text: RESULTS: Mammography shows a smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The smooth, polylobulated appearance on mammography is reassuring, but the rapid growth warrants further characterization to rule out a phyllodes tumor or other fibroepithelial lesions. REQUEST TEST: Core_Needle_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Microscopic description shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy findings of leaf-like structures with stromal overgrowth are classic for a phyllodes tumor. To determine if it is benign, borderline, or malignant, we need to assess the stromal cellularity and atypia more closely. REQUEST TEST: Histopathology_Review_for_Stromal_Cellularity

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal stromal cellularity and atypia confirm this is a benign phyllodes tumor, which explains the rapid growth despite the benign histology. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Phyllodes Tumor
